You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The crystal is described in an orthorhombic primitive cell with lattice parameters a = 4.01242 Å, b = 4.046011 Å, and c = 7.926225 Å, with all three interaxial angles equal to 90°. The structure belongs to space group Pmmm (number 47), with Hall symbol -P 2 2, and the input cell coincides with the standard cell: the relation q_standard = P q_input + s uses the identity matrix for P and a zero origin shift, so the input fractional coordinates are already the standard fractional coordinates. The input cell contains 8 atoms with composition Zr2Pd3Rh3, and positional values are reported to six decimal places; no precision corrections are required.

The zirconium atoms occupy the 2q Wyckoff orbit, with representative position (0, 0, z) and z = 0.246587. Under the Pmmm symmetry this generates a second Zr atom related by the mirror plane perpendicular to c, giving the pair at (0, 0, 0.246587) and (0, 0, 0.753413), so the two Zr atoms lie on the a-axis edge line above and below the midplane of the cell.

Palladium is distributed over two inequivalent sublattices. The first is the 2t orbit with representative (1/2, 1/2, z) and z = 0.249409, producing atoms at (1/2, 1/2, 0.249409) and (1/2, 1/2, 0.750591), a pair centered on the vertical line through the middle of the ab face, at nearly the same heights as the Zr pair. The second palladium sublattice is the fixed 1g position at (0, 1/2, 1/2), a single atom on the b-axis edge midpoint at the cell midplane.

The three rhodium atoms each occupy a distinct fixed one-fold orbit: Rh at 1e is at (0, 1/2, 0), Rh at 1d is at (1/2, 0, 1/2), and Rh at 1b is at (1/2, 0, 0). Together with the 1g Pd atom, these fixed sites lie on the edge-midpoint lines of the orthorhombic cell: the 1b and 1e Rh atoms sit at the base and the 1d Rh and 1g Pd atoms at the midplane, alternating along the edges parallel to c at (1/2, 0, z) and (0, 1/2, z).

Overall, the structure can be viewed as layers perpendicular to c: near z ≈ 0.247 and z ≈ 0.753, Zr atoms sit at the cell corners in projection while Pd atoms sit at the face center in projection; at z = 0 the edge midpoints (1/2, 0, 0) and (0, 1/2, 0) are occupied by Rh; and at z = 1/2 those same projected positions are occupied by Rh and Pd respectively. All atomic positions are fully specified by the two free parameters z = 0.246587 for Zr(2q) and z = 0.249409 for Pd(2t), together with the four fixed one-fold sites, under the full symmetry of Pmmm.
